title: Reflex actions
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the whole nervous system, with reflexes as one short part, so it is broader than the dedicated reflex point this course needs.

draft.title: Reflex actions
card: A reflex is a fast, automatic response to a stimulus. You do not choose it or think about it first.
The path is: receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, effector. The effector is a muscle or gland that responds.
In many reflexes the message is passed on inside the spinal cord, without waiting for the brain. This makes the response quicker, which can protect the body from harm.
The brain is told at about the same time, so you become aware of the event just after the response has begun.
draft.remember: A reflex is quick and automatic because the spinal cord can respond before the brain is aware.

a.q: Why can a reflex such as pulling a hand off a hot pan be so fast?
opts: The message is passed on in the spinal cord, not the brain
The brain decides faster when a stimulus is painful
The message travels along the blood to the muscle
The muscle senses the heat and moves by itself
a.why: In a reflex the spinal cord passes the message from a sensory neuron to a motor neuron, so the response does not wait for the brain. The brain deciding faster is tempting, but a reflex does not rely on a decision.
a.clue: Think about where the message turns around.

b.q: Leila steps on a sharp shell on a beach near Torquay. Her leg jerks up before she feels the pain. Which order shows the path of the message?
opts: Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, muscle
Receptor, motor neuron, brain, sensory neuron, muscle
Receptor, sensory neuron, brain, motor neuron, muscle
Muscle, motor neuron, spinal cord, sensory neuron, receptor
b.why: The message goes from the receptor along a sensory neuron to the spinal cord, then along a motor neuron to the muscle. The pain is felt after, when the brain is told. The option with the brain in the path describes a thought-out action, not a reflex.
b.clue: The leg moved before she felt pain.

wants.brief: A reflex arc: a receptor in the skin, a sensory neuron to the spinal cord, a motor neuron out to a muscle (the effector), with a short branch up to the brain. Label each part with the card's names.
wants.why: Seeing the path shows why the message can turn around in the spinal cord.

a.best: The message is passed on in the spinal cord, not the brain

b.best: Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, muscle
